title: Left ventricle wall is 6–7 times right's, matching the pressure ratio

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Left ventricle wall is 6–7 times right's, matching the pressure ratio

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The left ventricle requires six to seven times the dilating pressure of the right, and its wall thickness is greater in the same proportion.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we find (1) that we have had to use a pressure in the left ventricle from six to seven times as great as in the right ventricle, and (2) that the thickness of the walls is just in the same proportion.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Wall thickness of the heart”. Scope: mammalian hearts

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.79

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both quantities and the numerical criterion are unambiguous. Public human data can test important portions, but matched records and broad healthy mammalian coverage are limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate left:right ventricular systolic pressure and matched wall-thickness ratios in mammalian hearts. Ratios near six to seven in both measures support the claim; discordant or systematically different ratios refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched invasive pressures and images are uncommon.

Species and disease state strongly affect ratios.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both halves of the claim are numerical, so a large human sample can confirm or reject the factor of six to seven. Open MRI supplies the thickness ratio directly, and published catheterization series supply the pressure ratio for the same species. Other mammals are less uniformly measured, but a systematic departure in humans would already refute the proportion as a general mammalian fact.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate mean left-ventricular and right-ventricular wall thickness in the same hearts and compare their ratio with the ratio of systolic cavity pressures. The claim is confirmed if both ratios fall near 6-7 and match each other; a thickness ratio far from the pressure ratio, or either ratio far from 6-7, refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Where along the wall the thickness is taken changes the ratio.

Ventricular pressure ratios are widely tabulated in clinical series and are weakly paired with the same open imaging files.

fields.value:

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In normal mammalian (here human) hearts the left-ventricular wall is six to seven times as thick as the right-ventricular wall, and the left-ventricular systolic pressure is six to seven times the right, so the two ratios match.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py fetches and checksums the sources, averages the published per-sex mean muscle thickness of the LV anterior, lateral and inferior walls (septum excluded) and of the RV anterior, lateral and inferior walls (outflow tract excluded) from Westaby et al. Table 2, and takes the ratio. For pressure it takes the median of each person's mean systolic reading in NHANES 2017-2018 adults aged 20-59 not taking antihypertensive medication, by sex, and divides by the 20 mmHg midpoint of the healthy RV systolic range parsed from PMC9487613 Table 1 (bounds from 15 and 25 mmHg). Ratios are compared with the pre-registered intervals.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Thickness ratio R_t = (mean LV free-wall thickness) / (mean RV free-wall thickness), computed separately for males and females from the published per-sex means of morphologically normal autopsy hearts (Westaby et al. 2022, Cardiovasc Pathol, n = 1,062); LV free wall = mean of the reported LV wall sites excluding the septum; RV free wall = mean of the reported RV wall sites excluding the outflow tract. Pressure ratio R_p = median systolic blood pressure of NHANES 2017-2018 adults aged 20-59 not taking blood-pressure medication (brachial systolic as the proxy for LV peak systolic pressure) divided by 20 mmHg, the midpoint of the healthy-subject RV systolic range 15-25 mmHg (Table 1 of PMC9487613), with the range ends 15 and 25 reported as bounds. SUPPORTS if, for both sexes, R_t is in [5.0, 8.5], R_p is in [5.0, 8.5] and R_t / R_p is in [0.75, 1.33].

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. REFUTES if, for both sexes, R_t < 4.5 or R_t > 9.5, or R_t / R_p is outside [0.6, 1.67] (thickness not 'in the same proportion' as pressure). Any other outcome is MIXED. If the autopsy table cannot be obtained: inconclusive (data-unavailable).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: ratio of mean LV free-wall to mean RV free-wall muscle thickness in normal autopsy hearts (mean of female and male ratios)

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: female 4.024, male 3.936; per-site SDs 1.0 mm (RV) and 2 mm (LV)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's figures come from applying Laplace's law to the two ventricles; we test whether real hearts have the stated wall-thickness ratio and whether it matches the real pressure ratio. 'Thickness of the walls' is free-wall thickness measured at autopsy (the septum is shared by both ventricles and excluded). Peak LV systolic pressure is approximated by brachial systolic pressure (close in healthy adults without aortic stenosis); RV systolic pressure is not available as a public per-person dataset, so the published healthy range is used. Scope is 'mammalian hearts'; only human data are used, which can refute a general mammalian proportion but cannot confirm it for other species. Disclosure: before this pre-registration, web-search snippets shown while locating datasets displayed summary values from these sources (autopsy LV wall about 12 mm and RV walls about 2.7-3.6 mm; RV systolic 15-25 mmHg). The thresholds above are set from the claim's stated 6-7 with symmetric tolerance, not from those values.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
Westaby JD, Zullo E, Bicalho LM, Anderson RH, Sheppard MN. Effect of sex, age and body measurements on heart weight, atrial, ventricular, valvular and sub-epicardial fat measurements of the normal heart. Cardiovasc Pathol 2023;63:107508, Table 2

NHANES 2017-2018 Blood Pressure (BPX_J), Blood Pressure & Cholesterol questionnaire (BPQ_J) and Demographics (DEMO_J), CDC National Center for Health Statistics

Right heart catheterisation: best practice and pitfalls in pulmonary hypertension (Eur Respir Rev 2015;24), Table 1, RVP range in healthy subjects

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The pressure half of the claim holds: median systolic pressure is 5.7 (female) to 6.0 (male) times the 20 mmHg RV midpoint, inside Thompson's 6-7 band given the RV range (4.6-8.0). The thickness half fails: the LV free wall is only about 4.0 times as thick as the RV free wall in both sexes (11.0 vs 2.7 mm; 12.3 vs 3.1 mm), below the pre-registered 4.5 limit, so the walls are not 'in the same proportion' as the pressures (ratio of ratios 0.65-0.71).

A Laplace-law argument predicts wall thickness proportional to pressure times radius; the RV is crescent-shaped with a larger radius of curvature, so a thickness ratio below the pressure ratio is expected physiologically. That is a reason the claim fails, not a flaw in the test.

Autopsy wall thickness is measured post mortem, when the heart is in rigor or relaxed and wall thickness can differ from life by several millimetres for the LV (Hamburg study, PMC12018510); RV values are coarse (1 mm resolution, many readings of 2-3 mm). A 1 mm error in RV thickness moves the ratio by about a third, but a ratio of 6 would need the RV wall to be about 2 mm, below the reported medians at every site.

The autopsy cohort consists of sudden-death referrals with morphologically normal hearts, not a random population sample; the pressure data come from a different (US) population, and the RV pressure is a published normal range rather than measurements in the same people.

Only human hearts were used. The claim's scope is mammalian hearts; other species were not tested.

preregistered_at is the time of the pre-registration commit (2b1e5045); the committed pre-registration carried an estimated time (21:40Z) written before committing. Data were first downloaded after that commit; criteria are unchanged.
